key_insight: Constraining the steady conserved Allen–Cahn residual controls topology interface bandwidth intrinsically, without external density filters.
engineering_relevance: The approach suppresses single-node hinges and strut fragmentation while producing binarized designs with competitive stiffness.
method: Enforce the Allen–Cahn equality residual using a mass-weighted augmented Lagrangian method coupled with MMA.
Project the chemical potential to eliminate the constant residual mode and maintain compatibility with prescribed volume targets.
Exploit a symmetric-plus-rank-one Jacobian for matrix-free residual sensitivities without additional adjoint PDE solves.
evidence_signal: Across 48 benchmark cases, volume-preserving binarized designs matched or exceeded SIMP stiffness in 45 cases and averaged 1.2% stiffer; reported 3D residual-sensitivity overhead was 0.11% of the elasticity solve time.
watch_item: Diffuse designs showed 1.4%–12.3% higher compliance, so stiffness gains should be interpreted in the context of the volume-preserving binarization audit.
paper_title: Allen--Cahn Residual-Constrained Topology Optimization via an Augmented Lagrangian Method
